![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14264509/assets/0e2f2a41a551f21727825514a83dd8a0df4b45d8ea790f05e1e63d6a6e784526.png)

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2}f(x)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-17509.worked_solution:
To graph the function $y=\frac{1}{2}f(x),$ we take the graph of $y=f(x)$ and compress it by factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $2.$

The resulting graph is the solid blue curve shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14264509/assets/9da2a1ea570da8dcdf011e92967a78d1cc5cbee6f02ec1dce16d6b3dee8fd9df.png)

q-26449.name: Question 3
q-26449.problem: The point $P$ with coordinates $(4,0)$ lies on the curve $y=f(x).$ Which of the following points must lie on $y=4f(x)?$
q-26449.worked_solution:
The function $y=4f(x)$ represents a stretch of the function $y=f(x)$ by a factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis. This has the effect of multiplying the $y$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(x)$ by $4.$

Therefore, the point $(4,0)$ on $f(x)$ is mapped to the point $(4,4\cdot 0)=(4,0),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=4f(x).$
